SENIOR PRODUCT DATA ANALYST
Harborline Health — Chicago, IL or Remote (United States)

ABOUT HARBORLINE HEALTH

Harborline Health is a fictional B2B healthcare software company that helps
outpatient care teams coordinate referrals, scheduling, and patient follow-up.
Our product organization is expanding its analytics practice so that product,
engineering, operations, and clinical partners can make faster, evidence-based
decisions.

THE ROLE

We are hiring a Senior Product Data Analyst to own analytics for our Patient
Access product area. You will partner with a product manager, engineering lead,
designer, and operations stakeholders. The successful candidate will convert
ambiguous product questions into measurable hypotheses, trustworthy metrics,
and clear recommendations.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

- Build reproducible analyses and decision-support datasets using advanced SQL
  and Python.
- Define product metrics and create self-service dashboards in Looker or a
  comparable business intelligence platform.
- Design and analyze A/B tests, quasi-experiments, and funnel analyses; explain
  assumptions and limitations to non-technical partners.
- Partner with product managers to translate ambiguous business questions into
  measurable hypotheses and analysis plans.
- Present recommendations to product, engineering, operations, and executive
  stakeholders, including when the data does not support the proposed idea.
- Improve analytics reliability through version control, peer review,
  documentation, and automated data-quality checks.
- Mentor analysts on experimental design, metric definition, and stakeholder
  communication.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- 5+ years of professional experience in product analytics, data analytics, or
  a closely related role, including at least 2 years supporting a digital
  product team.
- Advanced SQL skills, including complex joins, window functions, and query
  optimization on a cloud data warehouse such as BigQuery or Snowflake.
- Proficiency in Python for analysis, automation, or statistical modeling.
- Hands-on experience designing experiments and interpreting statistical
  results for product decisions.
- Demonstrated ability to communicate a complex analysis as a concise business
  recommendation for both technical and non-technical audiences.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Experience with dbt, Airflow, or another analytics engineering or workflow
  orchestration tool.
- Experience working with healthcare, regulated data, or privacy-sensitive
  products.
- Familiarity with causal inference methods beyond standard randomized tests.

SUCCESS IN THE FIRST SIX MONTHS

- Establish a trusted activation funnel and metric definitions for Patient
  Access.
- Deliver at least one experiment or quasi-experiment that changes a product
  decision.
- Reduce recurring manual analysis by publishing reusable datasets and
  self-service reporting.

HIRING PROCESS

The interview process includes a recruiter conversation, a hiring-manager
discussion, a practical analytics case, and a cross-functional panel. Harborline
Health is an equal opportunity employer. This teaching example is fictional and
does not represent a real company or open role.

# Maya Chen

Chicago, IL · maya.chen@example.test · linkedin.example.test/mayachen

## Product Data Analyst

Product analyst with 6 years of experience turning product and operational data
into decisions for B2B SaaS teams. Strong in SQL, Python, experimentation,
metric design, and cross-functional communication. Experienced in ambiguous,
fast-moving product environments; new to healthcare analytics.

## Core Skills

SQL, Python, pandas, statistics, A/B testing, funnel analysis, cohort analysis,
Looker, Tableau, BigQuery, Airflow, Git, stakeholder presentations, product
metrics, data-quality monitoring

## Experience

### Senior Product Analyst — Meridian Works
Chicago, IL · March 2022–Present

- Owned analytics for the onboarding and collaboration surfaces of a B2B
  workflow product used by approximately 18,000 monthly active users.
- Rebuilt the activation funnel in BigQuery and Looker, resolving inconsistent
  metric definitions across product and revenue teams and reducing recurring
  reporting preparation from six hours to under one hour per week.
- Designed and analyzed seven controlled experiments. One onboarding experiment
  increased team activation by 8.4% and informed the next-quarter roadmap.
- Used Python and SQL to create a reusable retention-analysis pipeline scheduled
  through Airflow; added anomaly checks that caught two upstream tracking
  regressions before executive reporting.
- Partnered with product managers and designers to turn broad questions such as
  “Why do teams fail to collaborate?” into measurable hypotheses, event-tracking
  plans, and segmented analyses.
- Presented a recommendation to pause a proposed notification feature after the
  analysis showed no improvement in retention and a meaningful increase in user
  opt-outs.
- Mentored two analysts on experiment review, metric definitions, and concise
  executive communication.

### Data Analyst — Atlas Market Systems
Boston, MA · July 2019–February 2022

- Developed SQL models and Tableau dashboards for marketplace supply, demand,
  and service-quality metrics across 12 metropolitan areas.
- Built Python notebooks for cohort analysis and forecasting, replacing several
  spreadsheet-based monthly processes.
- Analyzed a phased pricing rollout using matched-market comparisons when a
  fully randomized test was not operationally feasible.
- Worked with engineering to document event definitions and investigate missing
  or duplicated product telemetry.
- Facilitated monthly reviews with product, finance, and operations leaders and
  translated findings into prioritized follow-up questions.

## Selected Project

### Volunteer Analytics Lead — Community Food Network
2023–Present

- Created a privacy-conscious reporting workflow using de-identified service
  records and role-based access to help program leaders understand appointment
  completion and wait times.
- The project involved sensitive community-service data, but it did not involve
  protected health information or healthcare regulatory compliance.

## Education

B.S. in Economics and Applied Mathematics — Northeastern University, 2019

## Additional Information

- Comfortable reviewing Git pull requests and writing basic automated checks.
- Has used Airflow in production but has not used dbt professionally.
- Has not worked for a healthcare company and has limited direct experience with
  formal privacy or regulatory frameworks.
perfect_resume_analytics_case.interview_round: My next round is a 60-minute live analytics case with a Hiring Manager and a Senior Product Analyst. It will focus on analytical frameworks, hypothesis testing, and explaining trade-offs and limitations aloud.
